items.readable_text:
Content:
Suppose that we want to solve the quadratic equation

Content:
[MATH: 2x^2-3x+1=0.]

Content:
To do this, we need to factor the trinomial on the left-hand side. We'll need to find two numbers such that

Content:
- their product is equal to the product of the quadratic coefficient and the constant (which is [MATH: 2 \times 1 = 2]), and
- their sum is equal to the linear coefficient (which is [MATH: -3]).

Content:
These two numbers are [MATH: -1] and [MATH: -2.] So, we can factor the left-hand side as follows:

Content:
[MATH: 2x^{2} − 3x + 1|= 0; 2x^{2}− 1x − 2x_(⏟)_(− 3x) + 1|= 0; (2x^{2} − x) + (− 2x + 1)|= 0; x(2x − 1) − 1(2x − 1)|= 0; (x − 1)(2x − 1)|= 0]

Content:
Applying the zero product rule, we have

Content:
[MATH: x-1=0 \qquad\text{or}\qquad 2x-1=0,]

Content:
which in turn gives

Content:
[MATH: x=1 \qquad\text{or}\qquad x=\dfrac{1}{2}.]

Content:
Therefore, the solutions are [MATH: x=\dfrac{1}{2},1.]

items.title: Solving When the Terms Have No Common Factor

sections.normalized_html:
First, we multiply by [MATH: -1] so that the leading coefficient becomes positive.

[MATH: − 2x^{2} + 9x − 4|= 0; (− 1) ⋅ (− 2x^{2} + 9x − 4)|= (− 1) ⋅ 0; 2x^{2} − 9x + 4|= 0]

To factor the left-hand side, we need two numbers that multiply to [MATH: 2 \cdot 4 = 8] and add to [MATH: -9.] These two numbers are [MATH: -1] and [MATH: -8,] so we can factor the left-hand side as follows: [MATH: \eqalign{ 2x^2 -9x +4 &=0\ 2x^2 -1x - 8x +4 &=0 \ (2x^2 -1x) + (-8x +4) &= 0\ x(2x-1) -4(2x-1) &= 0\ (2x-1)(x-4) &=0 }]

Applying the zero product rule, we have

[MATH: 2x-1=0 \qquad\text{or}\qquad x-4=0,]

which in turn gives

[MATH: x=\dfrac{1}{2} \qquad\text{or}\qquad x=4.]

Therefore, the solutions are [MATH: x=\dfrac{1}{2},4.]

sections.normalized_html:
First, notice that [MATH: 45], [MATH: 24] and [MATH: 36] have a common factor of [MATH: 3.] So, we can divide by [MATH: 3] to simplify our equation:

[MATH: (45x^{2} + 24x − 36)/(3)|= (0)/(3); (45)/(3)x^{2} + (24)/(3)x − (36)/(3)|= (0)/(3); 15x^{2} + 8x − 12|= 0]

To factor the left-hand side, we need two numbers that multiply to [MATH: 15 \cdot (-12)=-180] and sum to [MATH: 8.] These two numbers are [MATH: −10] and [MATH: 18,] so we can factor the left-hand side as follows: [MATH: \eqalign{ 15x^2 +8 x -12 &=0\ 15x^2 -10x +18 x -12 &=0 \ (15x^2 -10x) + (18 x -12) &= 0\ 5x(3x-2) + 6(3x-2) &= 0\ (5x+6)(3x-2) &=0 }]

[MATH: 5x+6=0 \qquad\text{or}\qquad 3x-2=0,]

which in turn gives

[MATH: x=-\dfrac{6}{5} \qquad\text{or}\qquad x=\dfrac{2}{3}.]

Therefore, the solutions are [MATH: x=-\dfrac{6}{5}, \dfrac{2}{3}.]

Item 5 — Example: Solving When the Terms Have a Common Factor

EXPLANATION

Explanation:

15x^2 +8 x -12 &=0\
15x^2 -10x +18 x -12 &=0 \

5x(3x-2) + 6(3x-2) &= 0\

}]

Applying the zero product rule, we have

[MATH: 5x+6=0 \qquad\text{or}\qquad 3x-2=0,]

which in turn gives

[MATH: x=-\dfrac{6}{5} \qquad\text{or}\qquad x=\dfrac{2}{3}.]

Therefore, the solutions are [MATH: x=-\dfrac{6}{5}, \dfrac{2}{3}.]
